title: TSMC OIP Ecosystem Forum 2026: Spotlight on Emerging Technologies - Semiwiki
gist: At TSMC's 2026 OIP Ecosystem Forum, six startups in the new Emerging Technologies Alley showcased agentic chip design, AI-native design services, UCIe/ONFI IP and physics AI for packaging; ChipAgents claims 200+ customers and Ricursive names Nvidia as a customer.

insights.claim: Agentrys positions itself as a tool builder rather than a tool provider, letting customers construct their own multi-agent frameworks while also shipping out-of-the-box solutions for design verification, root cause analysis and RTL generation.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Dual product model (platform plus turnkey) is a differentiator in the crowded agentic EDA field.

insights.claim: Agentic design flows are on the rise and many vendors offer them; Agentrys's claimed uniqueness is custom agentic flows that keep learning and improve with every design.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Watch whether learning-per-design creates switching costs in EDA.
insights.quote: Agentic design flows are on the rise.

insights.claim: ChipAgents is working with TSMC to jointly define the next-generation spec-to-GDS agentic design flow and reports more than 200 customers, which the author calls spectacular growth.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A foundry co-defining the agentic flow with a startup signals where EDA standards may form.

insights.claim: Silimate targets PPA optimization on TSMC technology with an autonomous system that ingests customer collateral, claiming customers can converge to PPA targets and fix functional bugs in days instead of months.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Time-to-tapeout compression is the core value metric for AI EDA vendors.
insights.quote: converge to your PPA targets and fix functional bugs in days instead of months

insights.claim: Ricursive Intelligence sells an end-to-end AI-native chip design service to companies with a custom-chip vision but no design team, claiming RTL-to-GDS in minutes using tools built from the ground up and tuned on each customer's data.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: AI-native design services could widen the pool of firms able to build custom chips.

insights.claim: Nvidia is the only customer Ricursive Intelligence can currently name, and the author treats Nvidia's use of its technology to extend an already advanced hardware team's productivity as a strong endorsement.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Single-reference traction; verify further customer wins before drawing conclusions.

insights.claim: Vinci offers a physics AI foundation model combining AI acceleration with FEA solver accuracy for full manufacturing-resolution simulation, targeting thermal and thermo-mechanical issues tied to advanced packaging.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Packaging-driven physics problems create a new AI-simulation niche adjacent to EDA.

insights.claim: Rising design complexity forces thermal, mechanical, performance and manufacturing issues to be addressed holistically and early, to avoid late surprises such as package warpage weeks before product introduction.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Earlier multiphysics analysis reduces costly late-stage rework and schedule risk.
insights.quote: the nightmare of discovering something like package warpage weeks before product introduction

insights.claim: The author argues that shifting accurate multiphysics analysis left lets designers find a better approach, not only optimize the current one, which he says has significant implications.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Implies design-space exploration value beyond defect avoidance.

insights.claim: Inspy was the lone IP provider in TSMC's Emerging Technologies Alley, offering ONFI PHY IP for NAND Flash and PHY and controller libraries for UCIe 3.0.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Chiplet interconnect IP demand is broadening beyond the largest IP vendors.

insights.claim: UCIe variants map to package types: UCIe-S for MCM packages with balanced performance and power, UCIe-A for advanced packages such as CoWoS, InFO and EMIB, and UCIe-3D for next-generation 3D stacking.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Useful mapping for assessing which interconnect IP fits which packaging platform.

insights.claim: TSMC introduced Emerging Technologies Alley at its 2026 OIP Ecosystem Forum, inviting six emerging companies (five design technology firms, one IP firm) to exhibit, with four of the five design firms focused on AI or agentic design.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: TSMC's curation signals which AI-design startups it sees as strategic ecosystem partners.

insights.claim: Startups emphasize close TSMC relationships to leverage its technology and ecosystem, suggesting foundry alignment is a key go-to-market lever for AI EDA entrants.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Foundry-certified flows may determine which startups scale.
